answer: Running a farm therefore means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. Because the age is read from the nectar checkpoint rather than self-declared, the sparrow audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 5 epochs old on the tundra ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 6 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
